title: Set difference of two measures as an integral of the density minus one
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$ with $\mu$ absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$ (that is, $\mu \ll 
u$), and let $S \subseteq \Omega$. Writing $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the (real-valued) Radon–Nikodym derivative of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$, one has
\[
  \mu(S) - 
u(S) \;=\; \int_{S} \left(  rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) - 1 ight) d
u(x).
\]
